chunks: Mālik, what a man Mālik was!
By Allāh, if he had been a mountain he would have been a big one (find), and if he had been a stone he would have been hard; no horseman could have reached it and no bird could have flown over it.

key_terms.الْحَافِرُ: The hoof (metonymy for a horseman or cavalry)
key_terms.صَلْداً: A hard, smooth, or bare stone (implying durability and lack of grip)
key_terms.فِنْداً: A large, massive, or prominent mountain
key_terms.مَالِكٌ: Mālik (proper name, referring to Mālik al-Ashtar)

ai.seo_question: What metaphors are used to describe Mālik al-Ashtar's physical strength and stature in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi records this vivid description of Mālik al-Ashtar’s imposing physique to highlight the physical manifestation of his inner strength and readiness for leadership, a key trait for a general in the early Islamic era. The metaphors of the mountain and stone underscore not just his durability but his steadfastness in battle, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the physical and spiritual fortitude of the Ahl al-Bayt's loyal companions.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Mālik, what a man Mālik was!
By Allāh, if he had been a mountain he would have been a big one (find), and if he had been a stone he would have been hard; no horseman could have reached it and no bird could have flown over it.
